study type: Retrospective review of placental pathology data
exposure: Clinical UC compromise (variable decelerations, UC entanglement, prolapse, true knot)
outcome: Placental histological signs (decreased fetal blood flow, hypoxia, shallow placental implantation, amnion nodosum, pathomorphological placental abnormalities)

Clinical phenotypes (oligohydramnios, abnormal fetal heart rate tracing, abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers, nonmacerated stillbirth, multiple pregnancy, fetal growth restriction, gestational hypertension, polyhydramnios, induction of labor, cesarean section, macerated stillbirth, congenital malformations, abnormal 3rd stage of labor)
cohort: 5634 consecutive placentas from pregnancies, categorized into groups based on the presence of clinical umbilical cord compromise and/or morphological umbilical cord abnormality.
finding: The coexistence of clinical signs of umbilical cord compromise and abnormal morphological umbilical cord phenotypes was statistically significantly associated with placental histological signs of decreased fetal blood flow, hypoxia, shallow placental implantation, and/or amnion nodosum.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as a common clinical phenotype in pregnancies where both clinical and morphological umbilical cord compromise coexisted.
